decision: coding-python-data-architecture (renamed from coding-python-enforce-data-architecture-strict, no alias) holds only the Python mechanisms and opens with a section telling the reader to load bitranox:coding-data-architecture, where the generic rules it cites by number live once.

evidence.text: test_the_python_data_architecture_skill_holds_no_copy_of_the_generic_rules passes on the new text and the same check returns False on the pre-edit text; the retrieval probes in checklist-20261109-rename-and-slim.md answered Python and workflow questions from the two files.

reopen_if: A Python reader acts on this skill alone and misses a generic rule, or the generic skill's numbering changes and the Core Principle references here stop matching.
why: A second copy of the generic rules here would drift from the generic skill; the rename drops the enforce-strict wording so the name says what the skill covers.

anchors: so for one the switch from `is` to `==` changes nothing
decision: For a plain Enum parameter (no value mixin), switching is to == changes nothing; coerce with TheEnum(value) at the function's start and test the raw and unknown paths.

evidence.text: Python 3.14: CombineMode.XOR == 'xor' is False; CombineMode('xor') returns the member, CombineMode('nand') raises ValueError.

reopen_if: Python changes Enum equality so plain members compare equal to their values.
why: A plain Enum never equals its raw value, so an == fix kept the wrong branch for raw-string callers.

anchors: whose name map leaves some members out must refuse those
decision: An Annotated BeforeValidator/PlainSerializer pair whose name map covers a subset of an Enum refuses members without a wire name instead of passing every member through.

evidence.text: pydantic 2.14.3: pass-through built and dump raised PydanticSerializationError(KeyError); subset check refused at a loc ending in '[key]'.

reopen_if: Pydantic validates a PlainSerializer's domain at validation time.
why: A blanket member pass-through builds the model and defers the failure to model_dump_json as PydanticSerializationError.

anchors: brief it to build a before/after output harness BEFORE its first edit
decision: A fixer changing a type on an output wire builds the before/after output harness before its first edit; git stash or checking out HEAD later is no baseline while sibling fixers share the checkout.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: a 548-run capture harness built before the edit was the only proof of zero output change.

reopen_if: Fixers each run in their own worktree, so a clean before-state stays reachable.
why: With parallel fixers in one checkout, a stash removes their uncommitted work mid-run; only a harness captured first proved zero output difference.

decision: Read a value_error item's validator message as str(item.get('ctx', {}).get('error')) under pyright strict.

evidence.text: pyright strict with pydantic 2.14.3 / pydantic_core 2.50.4: item['ctx'] reported 'Could not access item in TypedDict'; the .get form passed.

reopen_if: pydantic_core makes ctx a required key of ErrorDetails.
why: ctx is NotRequired in pydantic_core ErrorDetails, so the subscript form fails pyright strict.

anchors: Write the key only while it
Name that remaining downgrade window in the CHANGELOG
decision: A new field on a persisted model that earlier releases parse with extra=forbid is written only while it holds data (model_dump_json(exclude={key}) when empty), its absence is pinned in a test against a copy of the earlier model, and the remaining downgrade window is named in the CHANGELOG. exclude_unset and exclude_defaults are named as the wrong tools.

evidence.text: pydantic 2.14.3: an extra=forbid model refused {"history":["a"],"pending":[]} with extra_forbidden at ('pending',) and accepted the dump made with exclude={'pending'}; exclude_unset kept "pending":[] after a loaded key was cleared; exclude_defaults dumped a default State() as {}. The SKILL.md code block was executed and asserted on. Origin: a queued lesson where adding a key made the previous release lose its history.

reopen_if: Pydantic gains a per-field 'omit when empty' serialization setting that replaces the exclude call, or the project stops supporting downgrade.
why: An earlier release with extra=forbid refuses the whole file at the new key, losing its contents on downgrade. Writing the key only while non-empty keeps the common case readable.
